questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT a site of the Harappan / Indus Valley Civilisation?
questions.explanation: Pataliputra (modern Patna) was the Mauryan capital — much later than the IVC (2500-1700 BCE). Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are in present Pakistan. Lothal (Gujarat) was a major port of the IVC. Other Indian sites: Dholavira, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi.

questions.stem: The GREAT BATH — one of the most impressive public structures of the IVC — was found at:
questions.explanation: Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro (Sindh, Pakistan). Finely laid brick, gypsum plaster waterproofing, likely for ritual bathing. Excavated by John Marshall, R. D. Banerjee. Signals organised public life c. 2600 BCE.

questions.stem: Match the IVC SITE with its FEATURE. A. Lothal.  B. Kalibangan.  C. Dholavira.  D. Rakhigarhi. List-II: 1. Dockyard (earliest known).  2. Ploughed field + fire-altars.  3. Water-reservoir system + Harappan signboard.  4. Largest IVC site in India (in Haryana).
questions.explanation: Lothal (Gujarat) — dockyard. Kalibangan (Rajasthan) — ploughed field + fire altars. Dholavira (Gujarat) — elaborate water management + the 'Harappan signboard'. Rakhigarhi (Haryana) — largest IVC site in India.

questions.stem: The OLDEST of the Vedas is:
questions.explanation: Rigveda — oldest (c. 1500-1200 BCE), 10 mandalas, 1028 hymns. Samaveda — hymns for melodies. Yajurveda — sacrificial formulas. Atharvaveda — last and most 'folk' in content (medicine, magic, everyday life). Together called the CHATURVEDA.

questions.stem: The FAMOUS GAYATRI MANTRA is found in which text?
questions.explanation: Gayatri Mantra is from Rigveda (Mandala 3, Sukta 62, Mantra 10), composed by sage Vishwamitra, in praise of Savitr (the Sun). Considered the most sacred mantra in Hindu tradition.

questions.stem: The term 'Aryavarta' (land of the Aryans) in later Vedic texts refers broadly to:
questions.explanation: Aryavarta — the Sanskrit cultural-geographic term for the Indo-Gangetic Plain bounded by Himalayas (N), Vindhyas (S), Sindhu river (W), and Brahmaputra (E). Earlier Rigvedic Aryans mostly lived in the Sapta-Sindhu region (Punjab-Haryana). between Himalayas and Vindhyas.

_fixes.was: The Indo-Gangetic Plain (between Himalayas and Vindhyas)

questions.stem: The IVC SEALS commonly feature which mythical creature?
questions.explanation: The 'unicorn' — a one-horned bull — appears on more than 60% of IVC seals. Seals are typically 2-4 cm square, made of steatite (soapstone). Also common: humped bull (zebu), elephant, rhinoceros, tiger, Pashupati-like figure (on one famous seal).
